headline: Light rain spreads across the region this afternoon and tonight, bringing a much-needed 0.1 to 1 inch before tapering off Sunday morning, followed by cooler weather from Tuesday and rising rain chances Wednesday into Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain began this morning, but much of it is evaporating in dry air before reaching the ground; as the air moistens this evening and overnight, more of it will reach the ground in Charlotte and across the region, especially east of the mountains. Totals look like 0.10 to 1 inch, with the higher end wherever a heavier band sets up, currently most likely northeast Georgia and areas east of the mountains. Northeast winds gust roughly 15 to 30 mph east of the mountains through Sunday morning, while winds stay calm around Asheville.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Rain tapers off Sunday morning and the storm is gone by Sunday night, with low clouds around Charlotte starting to improve Sunday afternoon after about 2 PM. A cold front approaches Monday into Monday night, bringing warmer daytime temperatures first, though it may fall apart over the mountains and some moisture lingers across most of the area from Monday on. Cooler air filters in on Tuesday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Cooler temperatures stay in place through the end of the week. A pattern change sends a storm system from the south toward the region midweek, possibly with two low-pressure centers interacting and a new low forming near the coast, raising rain chances Wednesday into Thursday with lingering chances through at least Friday. A more northern track would mean less impact, a stronger, more southern track more rain, and if enough cold air is in place the higher mountain elevations could see a burst of wintry precipitation; forecasters say there are too many uncertainties to pin down details.

watch_for: How much of tonight's rain actually reaches the ground, with the best chance of up to an inch in northeast Georgia and east of the mountains.
The track of the midweek storm Wednesday into Thursday, which decides between more rain, less impact, or a burst of wintry weather in the higher mountains.
confidence: Forecasters expect rain tonight but amounts depend on how quickly the dry air moistens, and confidence in the midweek storm is low, with a lot likely to change.
